security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, documented Azure URLs, and placeholder environment variable examples. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, hidden command execution, or malicious network behavior in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Placeholder API key documentation can trigger secret scanners.
remediation.suggestion: State explicitly that AZURE_ANOMALY_DETECTOR_API_KEY must be supplied by the user and must never be committed.

remediation.issue: Example Azure Blob URLs include sasToken placeholders.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that sample SAS tokens are placeholders and production tokens should be scoped, short lived, and stored securely.

content.value_statement: Time-series anomaly detection in Java needs correct Azure SDK setup and model flow. This skill provides practical patterns for univariate, multivariate, streaming, and change point workflows.
actual_capabilities: Shows Maven dependency setup for the Azure AI Anomaly Detector Java SDK.
Demonstrates client creation with AzureKeyCredential and DefaultAzureCredential.
Provides univariate batch, last point, and change point detection examples.
Explains multivariate model training, batch inference, and last point detection flows.
Includes model listing, model deletion, and HTTP error handling patterns.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not run or validate Java code for the user.
It assumes the user already has an Azure Anomaly Detector resource and credentials.
It does not design production data pipelines, storage security, or alert routing.
Examples use placeholder data and need adaptation for real time-series schemas.

use_cases.title: Add Time-Series Monitoring
use_cases.description: Implement univariate batch or streaming anomaly checks for a metric already collected by an application.

use_cases.title: Train Multivariate Models
use_cases.description: Prepare the Azure SDK calls needed to train and run multivariate anomaly detection against correlated signals.

use_cases.title: Review Azure SDK Integration
use_cases.description: Check that client creation, credentials, polling, model management, and error handling follow common Azure Java patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Client
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a Java service
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to show how to create Azure AI Anomaly Detector Java clients with environment variables and safe credential handling.

prompt_templates.title: Detect Single Metric Anomalies
prompt_templates.scenario: Univariate detection for one time series
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a Java univariate anomaly detection flow for a daily metric with batch detection and last point checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multivariate Training
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan Java SDK calls for multivariate model training, inference data input, result polling, and contributor review.

prompt_templates.title: Harden a Production Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Java anomaly detection integration for credential handling, error handling, data source security, and model lifecycle gaps.

output_examples.input: I need to detect anomalies in one daily revenue series from Java.
output_examples.output: The assistant describes the univariate client setup, required time-series points, granularity selection, sensitivity tuning, and batch result handling.

output_examples.input: I have many correlated machine signals and need model training guidance.
output_examples.output: The assistant outlines data packaging, secure blob storage input, multivariate training, inference submission, polling, and contributor analysis.

output_examples.input: Review my Azure Anomaly Detector integration before production.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks environment variable use, Azure credential choices, error handling, SAS token handling, model cleanup, and monitoring boundaries.

best_practices: Store Azure endpoints and keys in environment variables or a managed secret store.
Match granularity, time range, and sensitivity settings to the actual metric behavior.
Use scoped, short lived storage access tokens for multivariate training and inference data.
anti_patterns: Do not commit Azure keys, SAS tokens, or service endpoints that expose real resources.
Do not train multivariate models with poorly aligned or sparsely sampled signals.
Do not treat anomaly scores as final incident decisions without domain review.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Java applications that call Azure AI Anomaly Detector for time-series anomaly detection workflows.

faq.question: Does it support univariate detection?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers batch detection, last point detection, and change point detection for single time series.

faq.question: Does it support multivariate detection?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows model training, batch inference, last point inference, result polling, and contributor interpretation.

faq.question: Does the skill include real Azure credentials?
faq.answer: No. It uses placeholder environment variable names and expects users to provide their own secure credentials.

faq.question: Can it validate my production data quality?
faq.answer: No. It can guide SDK usage, but users must validate real data quality, sampling, and operational thresholds.

faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
